keyChanges.title: Nevada NTA replaces 10-vehicle cap with 5,000-robotaxi Clark County permit
keyChanges.description: On August 20, 2026, the Nevada Transportation Authority unanimously approved Tesla's full Autonomous Vehicle Network Company permit, replacing the July 27 interim order that had capped Tesla at 10 vehicles on a Strip corridor at 45 mph with no airport pickups. The new permit authorizes up to 5,000 vehicles over 12 months in Clark County (Las Vegas metro). TeslaNorth reported the geofence includes Harry Reid International Airport and Henderson Executive Airport — reversing last week's airport ban. Tesla's Robotaxi account posted 'The golden future is upon us.' Cybercab engineering lead Eric Early told the NTA the permit is Clark County, not statewide, and that Tesla will 'hit the 5k the permit was approved for as soon as we possibly can.' In the same hearing, however, Early told commissioners 5,000 'has always been a ceiling' and 'I don't think we'll be in a position by this time next year to deploy 5,000 vehicles, and it's not [because of] the technology' — Tesla would be 'extremely happy' with 2,500. Tesla said it will start with a few Model Ys, not Cybercabs, after inspections, insurance, and fare filings expected within ~30 days. Waymo (1,000) and Uber via Motional/Zoox (1,000) received parallel paid-ride permits the same day. Zero Tesla robotaxis are in Las Vegas commercial service as of August 22. H1 2026 Las Vegas launch remains missed.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: The 10-to-5,000 cap reversal and airport inclusion are a genuine regulatory upgrade versus last week's interim order. Reality is still a paper permit: Tesla's own Cybercab lead said they will not fill 5,000 in 12 months, first vehicles will be Model Y not Cybercab, and no paid Las Vegas ride has been taken. Austin's year-plus failure to scale past ~20 unsupervised cars is the relevant prior.

keyChanges.title: Tesla sets Sept 3 Austin Cybercab launch event — paid public service still unconfirmed
keyChanges.description: Tesla began sending 'Exclusive Access' invitations on August 22 for a Cybercab Launch Event in Austin on September 3, 2026 (09.03.26). Official @Tesla graphics and influencer invite emails locked the date after a week of signaling: The Information reported August 17 that Tesla told staff a public Austin launch was targeting end of August, starting with employee rides on public roads then folding Cybercabs into the existing Model Y robotaxi service a few days later; Tesla's Robotaxi account launched a sweepstakes August 18 (rides through Aug 23, winners Aug 25) plus a mail-in entry to 1 Tesla Road. Austin first-responder training on how to move wheel-less Cybercabs was confirmed by a city spokesperson. TeslaNorth explicitly cautioned that September 3 is the event date, not a confirmed start of paid public Cybercab service. Teslarati hedged the same way: the milestone only matters 'if the event allows vehicles to take passengers on public roads.' As of August 22, zero Cybercabs are in paid commercial service. Production has been running since April (VIN floor #2172 / 2,000+ units claimed) while the entire unsupervised network still runs on Model Y. An invite-only influencer event plus employee public-road rides is not a commercial fleet launch.

The Information's own sourcing said the first public-road Cybercab passengers would be employees, with robotaxi integration 'a few days later' — still unconfirmed. keyChanges.title: Tesla tells JPMorgan it is holding back Model Y robotaxis to wait for Cybercab
keyChanges.description: JPMorgan analysts touring Fremont in August were told Tesla is 'intentionally holding back on adding Model Y units to the robotaxi fleet' because management is 'expressing confidence in its ability to scale Cybercab in the near-term.' Teslarati, NotATeslaApp, and Electrek all carried the note. That is a strategy confession, not a scaling proof: after more than a year of Model Y robotaxi operations, Tesla is freezing the only vehicle type actually carrying paid unsupervised riders in order to wait for a two-seater that has never taken a paid public fare. The unsupervised network remains stuck at roughly 21 active vehicles (Austin mixed; Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando, Tampa unsupervised; Bay Area safety-monitor) versus the abandoned H1 2026 target of 1,000+ across 7 cities. Tesla also told the bank it is targeting a long-run cost of ~$0.30 per mile with fleet expansion accelerating from late 2026 into early 2027 'if safety levels can allow it' — the same caveat that has blocked density for a year. FSD v15 details from the same meeting belong to the software category; the fleet implication does not: Tesla is choosing not to grow the live robotaxi fleet now.

keyChanges.title: Tesla IR tells JPMorgan Optimus sales slip to H2 2027; Fremont SOP still unconfirmed
keyChanges.description: JPMorgan's Rajat Gupta published a Fremont IR-meeting note around August 19–20, 2026 that restates Optimus as still pre-production while stretching the commercial date. Teslarati: Optimus 'remains on track for start of production in the coming months, with commercial sales possible as early as the second half of 2027.' Benzinga: Gen 3 commercial sales 'could begin by' H2 2027; the Gen 3 reveal will be held until closer to Fremont SOP 'to protect competitive advantage'; Gen 4 capability/cost/scale will be 'informed by Gen 3 field experience.' Electrek adds Tesla told the bank Gen 3 design is 'finalized,' the supply chain is 'essentially locked in,' and a line is going into the old Model S/X hall, with long-run capacity still pitched at ~1 million/yr Fremont and 10 million/yr Texas. Reality check: this is a delay, not a start. Q1 guidance was Fremont production in late July/August 2026 and first external customers late 2026. That window is gone with no official first-unit, rate, yield, or Academy delivery count. Q2 (July 22) was already softer — lines 'installing,' production 'soon'/'later this year,' first units for Optimus Academy training only, Musk saying 'there is no supply chain' and the S-curve's initial portion will be 'quite flat and long.' Four weeks later IR is selling 'supply chain essentially locked in' with no disclosed suppliers, BOM, or takt. Holding the Gen 3 reveal until SOP means Tesla still has not shown the production robot it promised for Q1 2026, then summer 2026. Gen 4 depending on Gen 3 field experience is circular when Gen 3 is not in the field. No robots doing useful factory work have been independently verified. Zero commercial units. Giga Texas dedicated factory remains a 2027 volume target.

keyChanges.title: IR restates FSD v15 as a step-change; still ~40% of tracks after 4 weeks, consumer on v14
keyChanges.description: Tesla IR told JPMorgan at a Fremont visit that FSD v15 is a 'step-change' in performance comparable to the leap from v13 to v14, built on seven core technologies, with roughly 40% of those already being tested in the robotaxi fleet and 'encouraging' early feedback. Consumer production FSD remains Supervised v14.3.7 (HW4) and v14.1 Lite (HW3) on software package 2026.21.6. Consumer v15 OTA remains an undated Q4 2026 / Q1 2027 target.

keyChanges.title: Unitree IPO hits $66B after selling 5,215 humanoids; Tesla Optimus still pre-revenue
keyChanges.description: Hangzhou-based Unitree Robotics, a direct Tesla Optimus competitor, listed on Shanghai's STAR Market on August 19, 2026. SCMP: shares opened 629% above the 150.80 yuan IPO price at 1,100 yuan, briefly valuing the company at ~445 billion yuan (~US$66 billion); they closed at 845 yuan (+460% day one, ~342 billion yuan / ~US$51 billion). Unitree sold 40.45 million shares and raised ~6.1 billion yuan. Benzinga, citing the same SCMP reporting, adds 2025 operating results: 1.7 billion yuan (~US$252 million) revenue, more than 4x the prior year; humanoids contributed ~868 million yuan (~US$129 million) vs quadrupeds ~698 million yuan; 5,215 humanoid robots and 23,037 quadrupeds sold, with overseas markets >40% of revenue. Chinese humanoid competitors (Unitree commercially shipping; BYD Xiao Di already showroom-deployed) are generating unit volume and listed-market capital while Tesla is still installing a first-gen Fremont line and hiding Gen 3. Caveat: Unitree's $66B open is IPO froth, not a proven Tesla-class AI stack, and G1-class hardware is not Optimus Gen 3. The relevant investor fact is commercial: Unitree already sold thousands of humanoids; Tesla has sold zero.

keyChanges.title: Einride orders 500 Tesla Semis — largest Semi deal, still a rounding error vs auto volume
keyChanges.description: On August 18, 2026, Swedish freight-tech company Einride AB (Nasdaq: ENRD) announced the world's largest public Tesla Semi commitment: 500 Class 8 trucks to be deployed on Einride's Saga AI platform for Amazon and other shippers across California, Texas, New Jersey, Illinois, and Georgia. First units are slated for September 2026, with the rest phased over 24 months and 'fully financed with third party financing solutions' — no lender or terms disclosed. Tesla Semi Director Dan Priestley confirmed the order. This beats WattEV's May 370-unit California port-drayage order and is the first Semi deal that looks like a real corridor deployment rather than a PepsiCo-style pilot. It does not change Tesla's auto P&L. At quoted US pricing of ~$260k Standard / ~$290k Long Range, the hardware bill is roughly $130–145 million. Einride closed June with only about $77 million in cash and booked $27 million of H1 2026 revenue with adjusted EBITDA of negative SEK 363 million; the $800 million 'ARR' figure Einride attached to the deal is pipeline under joint business plans, not contracted backlog. Five hundred trucks over two years is ~1% of the Nevada plant's 50,000-unit annual capacity and a rounding error versus Q2's 480,126 passenger deliveries. High-volume Semi production only started April 29, 2026, after a nine-year delay from the 2017 reveal; 2026 Semi deliveries remain estimated at 5,000–15,000 units, still constrained by 4680 cell output.

sentiment.rationale: Headlines call this Tesla's 'MASSIVE' Semi order. Reality: 500 trucks over 24 months, third-party financed, attached to $800M of unsigned pipeline ARR, and immaterial to Tesla's 1.65M-delivery auto business. It is a real commercial signal after years of pilots, not a volume inflection.

keyChanges.title: Korea FSD remains origin-split: Shanghai-built majority fleet still blocked despite 50M km
keyChanges.description: Tesla Korea announced on August 21, 2026 that Supervised FSD has logged 50 million cumulative kilometres on Korean roads — and simultaneously confirmed that this figure excludes the Shanghai-built Model 3 and Model Y that make up the bulk of Tesla's Korean sales. Those HW4 vehicles still cannot use Supervised FSD because Korean certification is origin-dependent: U.S.-built cars enjoy Korea-U.S. FTA treatment, while Chinese-built cars must meet domestic motor-vehicle safety standards. Article 111-3 of Korea's vehicle-performance rules requires an automated lane-keeping system to stay in-lane unless specified conditions are met, which collides with FSD's unsupervised lane-change behavior. Shanghai-built cars instead get a crippled 'Assisted Driving' / Navigate on Autopilot mode that requires the driver to hit the turn signal or touchscreen before any lane change. A National Assembly petition filed August 19 demanding identical certification standards regardless of production origin had ~7,900 signatures by August 21 — only 16% of the 50,000 needed for referral. MOLIT said on April 27 it has 'never blocked' FSD on Chinese-built Teslas and that Tesla can self-certify if it meets domestic standards, but also said Tesla Korea has made no separate request or meeting to apply FSD to Shanghai Model 3/Y. Two theoretical paths remain: Tesla de-features FSD to pass current Korean rules, or Korea transposes UNECE DCAS — neither of which Tesla has publicly initiated. The 50M km headline is therefore a minority-fleet marketing stat, not a market-wide approval.

sentiment.rationale: Headlines celebrate 50 million km of Supervised FSD in Korea. Reality is that the majority Shanghai-built fleet is still locked out by origin-based safety certification, Tesla has not even applied for self-certification of those vehicles, and MOLIT's lane-change rule is an unresolved legal block.

keyChanges.title: Giga Texas cathode video is a 10 GWh Early Ramp tour, not a 4680 GWh win
keyChanges.description: On August 21, 2026, Tesla North America posted the first interior video of the Giga Texas cathode plant, writing that Tesla is 'operating the first large scale cathode production facility in North America as part of our 4680 cell production in Austin, TX.' TeslaNorth and BASENOR both carried the clip. Headlines treat this as the cathode line going live. Reality: Tesla already flagged full-scale cathode commencement on the Q4 2025 call (January 28, 2026), and the Q2 2026 IR capacity table listed Texas cathode materials at 10 GWh with status Early Ramp — BASENOR restates that ~10 GWh starting figure. TeslaNorth is explicit that Tesla disclosed no tonnage, no utilization, no start-of-rate date, and no list of which vehicles already use Austin-coated cathode; treat the video as a plant tour, not a quarterly scoreboard. Dry-electrode anode+cathode was already claimed in mass production in January 2026. Q2 IR still named battery pack capacity as the limiting factor on global vehicle volume, with Texas 4680 at >40 GWh installed (not proven output) and Berlin 4680 still Construction with a blank capacity figure and 18 GWh expansion not due until H1 2027. A cathode walkthrough does not move 4680 yield, scrap, cost/kWh, or actual GWh shipped — none of which Tesla disclosed this week.

sentiment.rationale: Headlines frame a first-look video as large-scale cathode production going live. Tesla's own Q2 table already listed Texas cathode at 10 GWh Early Ramp, the Jan 28 call already claimed commencement, and Tesla still has not published 4680 yield or actual GWh while pack/cell capacity remains the stated global vehicle bottleneck.
